text:
Annie: quick thought — we should formalize route-affinity + version pinning for model selection. proposing header-driven rules: `x-model-alias` (logical alias), `x-model-pin` (optional exact version), and a compatibility check before commit.

Morgan: +1 on alias/pin. question: if `x-model-pin` is incompatible with route constraints (e.g. pinned quantized v2 not compatible with 8-bit execution), do we fail the request or fall back to alias-resolved candidate?

Annie: prefer fallback with clear reason codes. fail only if pin is "hard" (customer explicitly asked for hard pin). otherwise pick highest-priority compatible variant. record telemetry that pin was ignored.

Sasha: we need model capability metadata surfaced in the catalog (e.g., supports_kv_cache, supported_quantizations, max_seq). routing should match on a small capability set to avoid runtime errors. we could add a matcher syntax: `model.capabilities contains kv_cache && quantization in (q4_0,q4_k)`.

Ryan: +1. also add an ordered fallback list on the rule: `fallbacks: [alias:fast-approx, alias:fp16-safe, default]` so gateway knows which variants to try. and the gateway should emit `routing.decision` telemetry with fields: `route_id`, `chosen_model`, `reason` (pin|match|fallback|hard_fail).

Morgan: implementation debate — should we evaluate these matchers in the control plane (precompute candidate set & push to gateways) or do it in the API gateway at request time? doing it in the gateway is lower-latency for dynamic headers, but control plane centralizes policy. thoughts?

Sasha: hybrid: control plane validates and compiles rules to a compact matcher table. gateways receive compiled rules + model capability cache. gateway performs match at request time using header values. keeps policy centralized but runtime fast.

Annie: UX asks: console needs a route-preview tool that shows: sample request headers => matched model, why (pin/match/fallback), token cost estimate, and quota enforcement outcomes. also a canary slider for gradual rollouts.

Ryan: agree. for quotas, we should evaluate per-route token budget before selecting expensive variants (prevent head-of-line cost spikes). add `quota_budget_check` as a pre-match step.

Morgan: small API example for gateways:
```
POST /infer
Headers:
  X-Model-Alias: chat-moderation
  X-Model-Pin: chat-moderation@v3.1
  X-User-Tier: enterprise
```
Gateway evaluates compiled rules in this order: 1) hard pin check 2) quota_budget_check 3) capability match 4) fallbacks.

Sasha: also ensure response includes `X-Model-Used` and `X-Routing-Reason` for debugging. console should surface recent `routing.decision` events and counts of "pin ignored" vs "hard fail".

Annie: action items: (1) Sasha: add capability fields to model catalog + matcher grammar (PR by EOW) (2) Ryan: design telemetry schema + console wires for route-preview (mockups by Thurs) (3) Morgan: prototype compiled matcher table format + gateway lookup (POC next sprint) (4) infra-bot: ensure gateways get model capability cache invalidation hook.

infra-bot: deploy-notice: rolling config push scheduled 2026-04-02 03:00 UTC for compiled-matchers feature flag. will notify channels on rollout. :robot_face:

Morgan: one more note — document behavior for simultaneous pins: header pin vs route pin vs tenant-level pin. priority: header pin (if hard), tenant pin, route default, alias default. record final precedence in docs.

Annie: perfect. I'll draft the RFC with examples and include the failure codes list. thanks all :thumbsup:
